source.title: Protein Circuit Tracing via Cross-layer Transcoders
source.authors: Darin Tsui; Kunal Talreja; Daniel Saeedi; Amirali Aghazadeh

record.file_problem: Minor extraction issue: the opening text begins mid-word. The remainder includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Applies sparse latent representations to protein language models and reports task-performance and circuit results, extending interpretability evidence to ESM2. It does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results for sparse cross-layer transcoder latents and task circuits in ESM2, relevant to V4. It does not test feature competition, superposition geometry, or one-dimensional directions. Steering results are induced interventions and do not establish spontaneous superposition. Comparisons with cited prior SAE work are not treated as results of this study.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper. It trains TopK cross-layer transcoders on ESM2 and reports how well its replacement model and greedy-search circuits recover probe performance on protein tasks. The comparisons are mainly against per-layer transcoders, CAA and black-box optimizers. It assumes that sparse, interpretable latents exist and uses them as a tool. It never asks whether features are superposed, whether polysemanticity reflects capacity pressure, whether features are one-dimensional, or whether dictionary features are canonical. The recovery numbers show the method's fidelity, not evidence about superposition in ESM2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that cross-layer transcoders (ProtoMech) build a replacement model of ESM2 that recovers 82–89% of performance. They find compact circuits (<1% of latents) that align with biological motifs and can be steered toward high-fitness variants. They argue that SAEs only factorize single activation states and cannot serve as replacement models. They also report a denoising effect where circuits sometimes beat ESM2 on poorly performing tasks.
record.recipe_differences: Uses TopK cross-layer transcoders trained to approximate ESM2 MLP computations and identifies task-specific circuits; it does not use the original toy-network superposition setup or test feature geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Replacement strategy changes reported performance; the paper reports better results for direct or sequential replacements than for some alternatives, and lower performance for full replacements. These replacement-model comparisons do not test superposition geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: TopK cross-layer transcoders on ESM2 reconstruct MLP outputs with normalized MSE of about 0.13–0.15. They have k=16 or 24 active latents per layer and a 10x expansion. Their replacement models recover 82–100% of probe performance, versus 0.50 F1 for per-layer transcoders on ESM2-8M family tasks. Individual latents align with known motifs, such as HRD and the glycine-rich loop.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse cross-layer transcoders can faithfully approximate protein language model MLP computation with interpretable latents (a method-fidelity claim, not a superposition claim).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Evidence is limited to ESM2 protein-language models and the reported supervised tasks. Circuit discovery uses a hybrid replacement strategy that holds ground-truth attention outputs fixed; the paper notes that full replacement can suffer compounding reconstruction errors. The study does not directly compare SAE features or evaluate superposition geometry.
record.rows_left_out: Not applicable; all selected results relevant to V4 are included. Steering outcomes are omitted because they are induced interventions and do not test the claim versions.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All parts: no capacity or feature-importance analysis.

Whether ESM2 spreads features across neurons or stores more features than dimensions. Transcoder latents are assumed and used, not tested against a dense or neuron baseline as evidence of superposition.
Completeness, stability across seeds and canonicity of dictionary features. No SAE or transcoder comparison across runs or sizes.
All parts: no test of one-dimensional versus multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V4 'supports' labels are removed. The rows report the study's own method fidelity and thresholded circuit-search outputs, not evidence that ESM2 superposes features. The study is not an original source. Steering results are rightly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions; sparsity-dependent transitions; regular or near-orthogonal geometry.
Whether capacity pressure causes polysemanticity or whether important features get dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.

The study uses cross-layer transcoders, not SAEs; it studies ESM2 protein-language-model representations and supervised protein tasks, not general-purpose language models or feature spread across neurons.
The study discusses limits of SAE factorization for tracing computation but does not experimentally test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.subject: ESM2-8M
rows.operation_detail: Measured protein-family classification performance using all ProtoMech latents in the sequential replacement model.
rows.note: Reported as an average across protein-family classification tasks.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's fidelity: probe F1 recovered by the sequential replacement model. It does not measure superposition or feature spread.

rows.subject: ESM2-8M
rows.operation_detail: Measured protein-family classification performance using the discovered ProtoMech circuit in the sequential replacement model.
rows.note: Reported as an average across tasks; the paper says the circuit used 150 ± 204 latents on average.
rows.check: This is circuit fidelity from greedy search with a 70% stopping threshold. The value partly reflects that selection criterion. It is method performance.

rows.subject: ESM2-8M
rows.operation_detail: Measured the size of discovered protein-family circuits.
rows.value: 150 ± 204 latents on average; roughly 0.8% of the total possible latent space
rows.note: The reported circuit size is a sparse subset of the latent space.
rows.check: This is a selection value. Circuit size is the output of a greedy search that stops at 70% recovery, in batches of 32 latents. It is not a measure of the model's representation.
